rankings.howCalculatedIntro: Rankings are computed from five components plus a roster talent prior that tapers off as the season progresses. Each component is normalised relative to the rest of the league (best team = 1.0, worst = 0.0) before weighting, so rankings reflect where a team stands right now.
rankings.componentPointsDesc: Points earned divided by maximum possible (games played × 2). The primary measure of season-long success.
rankings.componentL10Desc: Same formula applied to the last 10 games only. This is what moves rankings week to week — a hot team climbs, a cold team falls regardless of earlier results.
rankings.componentGDDesc: Goals scored minus goals allowed per game. Teams that win convincingly rank higher than teams that constantly squeak by one goal.
rankings.componentXGFDesc: Expected goals for % at even strength — the share of shot quality a team generates versus allows at 5-on-5. Filters out goaltending and shooting luck that inflate or deflate raw goal totals.
rankings.componentSPDesc: Average of power play % and penalty kill %. Weighted lower than even-strength play because special teams frequency and opponent quality vary.
rankings.componentWARDesc: Sum of the top-18 skaters' Wins Above Replacement plus the starter's Goals Saved Above Expected. Weighted at 15% at game 0, tapering to 0% by game 20. Ensures pre-season and early-season rankings reflect roster quality rather than a handful of fluky results.
rankings.howCalculatedFootnote: xGF% and Roster WAR show — until the first nightly pipeline run populates them. All other components still produce a valid rank.

advanced.shotExplainFull: Corsi For% (CF%) approximates all shot attempts using shots on goal + blocked shots from the NHL realtime report. Fenwick For% (FF%) uses shots on goal only, excluding blocked shots. Both measure territorial control — ≥50% means {{abbr}} is generating more attempts than opponents.
advanced.shotExplainProxy: Shot For% is a SOG-based proxy. Realtime blocked shot data unavailable for this game type.
advanced.cfNote: All shot attempts for ÷ total. ≥50% = territorial control
advanced.ffNote: Unblocked attempts for ÷ total. Filters out shot-blocking luck
advanced.proxyNote: SOG for ÷ total SOG. ≥50% = outshooting opponents
advanced.blockedForNote: Shots blocked by {{abbr}} skaters per game
advanced.blockedAgainstNote: {{abbr}} shots blocked by opponents per game
advanced.possessionNote: Time with puck ÷ total play time
advanced.pdoExplain: PDO = team shooting% + save% × 100. League average = 100. Values above 102 suggest positive puck luck likely to regress; below 98 suggest negative luck. Useful for identifying unsustainable streaks.
advanced.netPpExplain: Net PP% excludes goals where the opposing team was also shorthanded simultaneously.
advanced.netPkExplain: Net PK% excludes goals while both teams were shorthanded simultaneously.

goalie.gsaxCaption: Goals saved above expected — flurry-adjusted xGoals model
goalie.tip5v5SvPct: Save percentage at even strength (5-on-5 only). Removes special teams situations which can skew overall SV%. The most stable indicator of true goaltending ability.
goalie.tipHdSvPct: Save percentage on high-danger shots — taken within ~15 feet of the net. The hardest shots to stop; the best quality-adjusted goalie metric.
goalie.tipMdSvPct: Save percentage on medium-danger shots (15–30 feet from net). Complements HD SV% for a fuller picture of save quality across shot locations.
goalie.tipPkSvPct: Save percentage while shorthanded. Penalty kill goaltending requires different positioning — some goalies are significantly better or worse in this situation than at even strength.

skater.warTip: Wins Above Replacement (beta). EV component uses 5v5 RAPM — ridge regression across 3 seasons of league-wide shift and shot data, controlling for teammates and opponents. PP/PK and finishing components are xGoals-based from MoneyPuck. RAPM is 5v5 only; special teams remain approximate. Zone-start adjustment in development — defensive defensemen may be slightly undervalued in current model. Validated periodically vs Evolving Hockey public RAPM.
skater.tipEvXgfPct: On-ice expected goals for % at 5-on-5. The share of total shot quality generated while this player is on the ice — above 50% means the team outshoots opponents in quality with him on the ice. Team metric, not individual.
skater.tipXgf60: Individual expected goals generated per 60 minutes — the shot quality this player personally produces, based on shot location and type. Measures how dangerous their own shots are, independent of linemates.
skater.tipXga60: On-ice expected goals against per 60 minutes at 5-on-5. Measures how many quality chances opponents generate while this player is on the ice — lower is better. Team metric reflecting the full line's defensive performance.
skater.tipHdca60: High-danger chances against per 60 minutes at 5-on-5. Shots from the slot and crease — the most likely to result in goals. Lower is better.
skater.tipGoals60: Goals scored per 60 minutes of ice time. Rate-adjusts for playing time so a player with 15 min/game and one with 22 min/game can be compared fairly.
skater.tipA160: Primary (first) assists per 60 minutes. First assists directly set up the goal scorer and are more meaningful than secondary assists, which can be coincidental.
skater.tipPpToi: Power play ice time this season. Presence here means the player has enough PP time for a reliable PP metric — see the Power Play percentile bar below.
skater.tipPkToi: Penalty kill ice time this season. Presence here means the player has enough PK time for a reliable PK metric — see the Penalty Kill percentile bar below.

resultsVsProcess.emptyState: Not enough games yet for a reliable read.
resultsVsProcess.emptyStateSub: Needs a minimum sample of games played this season.
resultsVsProcess.tipOnIceGf: On-ice goals-for percentage at 5-on-5 -- the share of goals scored (not just shot attempts/quality) while this player is on the ice. The 'results' side of this pairing.
resultsVsProcess.tipGapVsProcess: On-Ice GF% minus EV xGF% (the process/shot-quality side, shown above in the percentile rankings). A large positive or negative gap suggests results are running hotter or colder than the underlying process -- often a sign of unsustainable luck rather than true talent.

contract.valueTooltipBlended: Blended score: 60% points per $1M (projected to 82 GP) + 40% WAR per $1M (scaled). WAR uses 5v5 RAPM (beta) + PP/PK/finishing components — captures two-way value points miss. Defensive specialists and shutdown players score higher here than on a pure points basis. Scale: ≥8.0 Exceptional · ≥5.0 Great · ≥3.0 Good · ≥1.8 Fair · ≥1.0 Below avg · <1.0 Overpaid. ELC contracts excluded.
contract.valueTooltipPointsOnly: Points per $1M of cap hit (projected to 82 games). WAR data unavailable for this player — using points only. Scale: ≥8.0 Exceptional · ≥5.0 Great · ≥3.0 Good · ≥1.8 Fair · ≥1.0 Below avg · <1.0 Overpaid. ELC contracts excluded.
contract.p60Tip: Points per 60 minutes of ice time. Removes ice time differences — a player with 10 pts in 12 min/game produces at a very different rate than 10 pts in 22 min/game. League avg for top-6 forwards: ~2.0–3.5.
contract.elcTip: Entry Level Contracts have a league-mandated cap hit ($775K–$925K) that doesn't reflect market value, so the blended value comparison isn't meaningful.
contract.elcTipShort: ELC cap hits are league-mandated and don't reflect market value.
contract.goalieValueTip: Goals saved above expected (GSAX) per $1M of cap hit. GSAX accounts for shot quality and volume — a positive number means the goalie saved more goals than an average goalie would have on the same shots. Dividing by cap hit shows how much of that value you're getting per dollar. Scale: ≥4.0 Exceptional · ≥2.0 Great · ≥0.0 Fair · ≥-2.0 Below avg · <-2.0 Overpaid. ELC goalies excluded.

scratches.title: Scratches
scratches.infoTip: Players left out of the lineup, from the NHL's official game rosters. Each scratch is checked against that day's injury report: not on it means a healthy scratch (a coaching decision); on it means injured or suspended. Scratches before Sept 12, 2026 predate the injury history, so only their totals are known.
scratches.unavailable: Scratch data isn't available right now.
scratches.unclassifiedNote: Healthy vs. injured isn't known for these games — that split starts with games played from Sept 12, 2026 on.

playoffOdds.title: Playoff odds
playoffOdds.infoTip: How often this team makes the playoffs when the rest of the regular season is simulated 10,000 times. Each game's odds come from the two teams' Elo ratings (the same ones behind game predictions), with extra spread for how unsure those ratings are — more early in the season, less later. Updated nightly.
playoffOdds.earlyNote: Early season: these odds lean heavily on last season's ratings and will move a lot.
playoffOdds.none: Playoff odds appear after the first nightly model run of the season.
playoffOdds.unavailable: Playoff odds aren't available right now.

injuryImpact.title: Games lost to injury
injuryImpact.infoTip: Games missed this season by players on the injury report (day-to-day, out, or injured reserve) who didn't dress, checked against the NHL's official shift data. WAR lost adds up each player's wins-above-replacement per game (this season and last) for every game he missed. Goalies count in games lost but have no WAR here. Tracking starts with the 2026-27 season.
injuryImpact.rankTitle: League rank — #1 has lost the most
injuryImpact.method: A man-game lost is a game a player on the injury report didn't dress for. WAR lost = his WAR per game × games missed.
injuryImpact.none: Injury tracking starts with the first regular-season game.
injuryImpact.unavailable: Injury impact isn't available right now.

probableStarters.title: Probable starters
probableStarters.infoTip: Who's likely to start in goal, from each team's own pattern over the last three seasons: share of recent starts, who started last game, back-to-backs and rest. The NHL doesn't announce starters ahead of time, so these are estimates. Goalies listed out or on injured reserve are left out. Posted two days before the game and updated each morning.

methodology.title: How it works
methodology.intro: How the app's predictions are made and graded, and how its injury and trade data are built. Every prediction on the scorecard comes from one of the models below; when a model changes, the change is dated in the changelog at the bottom.
methodology.checkedNote: Settings described here were checked against the code on {{date}}. Backtest numbers come live from the scorecard.

principles.title: Ground rules
items: Predictions are written down before the game, by the nightly run at 3 AM Eastern, and graded afterward against what happened. The live record counts only those.
Each model is compared with a simple baseline anyone could use, so you can see whether it adds anything.
Backtests replay past seasons using only what was known at the time. They're always labeled as backtests, never as a track record.
These are probabilities, not picks. Nothing here is betting advice.
When a model changes, the change is dated below, so any prediction can be matched to the version that made it.

gameWinners.title: Game winners
body: Every team has an Elo rating built only from game results since the 2023-24 season. Teams start at 1,500, and after each game the winner takes rating points from the loser: more for an upset, fewer for an expected result.

A bigger regulation win moves ratings a little more (up to 1.75 times a one-goal win). A game decided in overtime or a shootout moves them half as much, since needing extra time says the teams were close. Each game moves ratings only slightly (K = 6), because one hockey game is noisy. Between seasons, every rating moves a third of the way back to 1,500.

The home team gets 35 Elo points before the win chance is worked out, except at neutral-site games: P(home wins) = 1 / (1 + 10^((away − (home + 35)) / 400)). These are FiveThirtyEight's published NHL Elo settings, not tuned on our own data.

Every regular-season and playoff game is logged by the 3 AM run on game day (and the day before, in case a run is missed). The last number before puck drop is the one graded, against the final result, overtime and shootouts included. The baseline is "the home team wins".

Tested and not adopted (September 2026): we replayed 2024-25 and 2025-26 with each night's actual lineups — more than any injury report could tell us ahead of time — adjusting each team for regulars who didn't dress (valued by last season's WAR) and for its starting goalie (by last season's goals saved above average). On games the adjustment wasn't fit on, missing skaters made the predictions no better, and the starting goalie improved them only slightly (Brier about 0.0004 lower), a gain that would shrink when the starter isn't known in advance. Neither is used; the goalie adjustment will be tested again during 2026-27, and any change will be dated in the changelog.
limits: Elo only knows results. It doesn't know about injuries, who's in goal, trades or lineup changes until they show up in results.
A team that changes a lot over the summer still carries two-thirds of last season's rating into October.

startingGoalies.title: Starting goalies
body: For each team's next regular-season game, once it's within two days, the candidates are the goalies on the current roster, minus anyone listed out or on injured reserve on the latest injury report.

Each candidate is scored on six things from his team's recent games: his share of the last 10 starts; whether he started the previous game; whether it's the second night of a back-to-back and he started the first night, or didn't; days since his last start; and whether he's gone 20 games without a start. A conditional logit model, fit on every start from 2023-24 through 2025-26, turns these into probabilities that add up to 100% for each team.

Share of recent starts and back-to-backs matter most; days of rest adds almost nothing once those are known. With his recent share known, a goalie who just started is slightly less likely to go again, because of tandems and rotations.

The number is updated each night until the game; the morning-of number is graded against who actually started, using the NHL's own starter flag. The baseline is "last game's starter starts again". In the backtest, each season is scored by a model fit only on earlier seasons.
limits: The NHL doesn't announce starters ahead of time, and the model can't see a coach's announcement or morning-skate reports.
A goalie listed day-to-day stays a candidate at full weight: the injury history only starts in September 2026, so the model has never learned what day-to-day means.
Preseason and playoff games aren't predicted.

playoffOdds.title: Playoff odds
body: Every remaining regular-season game is simulated 10,000 times. Each game's win chance comes from the same Elo ratings and home-ice edge as the game predictions.
22.1% of simulated games go past regulation, giving the loser a point — the share measured across 2023-24 to 2025-26.

Current ratings are only estimates, so each simulated season shifts every team's strength by its own random amount. That spread is widest before the season and narrows as games are played; without it the odds were overconfident (one team showed 95% before a game was played). How wide it starts and how fast it narrows were tuned on the 2023-24 to 2025-26 backtest.
In each simulated season the top three teams in each division and the next two best in each conference make the playoffs. Ties go to points, then regulation wins, then wins, then a coin flip.
Each day's change is explained game by game: the odds are stored for every possible result of the next day's games, so the next run can show how much each result moved them.
Graded: the odds as of the season's first run, Nov 15, Jan 1 and Mar 1, against who actually made the playoffs. The baseline is "whoever holds a playoff spot at that moment".
limits: Head-to-head and the later NHL tiebreakers aren't modeled.
Within a simulated season, ratings don't change beyond that one random shift, so a hot or cold streak isn't projected forward.
Like game winners, the ratings don't know about injuries or trades.

grading.title: How the scorecard grades
body: Picked right: the side given 50% or more is what happened.

Brier score: the average squared gap between the stated probability and what happened (1 if it happened, 0 if it didn't). 0 is perfect, and always saying 50% scores 0.25; lower is better. It rewards honest percentages, not just right picks: saying 90% and being wrong costs far more than saying 55% and being wrong.

Calibration: predictions are grouped into ten bands by stated probability and compared with how often they came true — a well-calibrated model's 70% calls happen about 70% of the time. Bands with fewer than 25 predictions aren't shown, since a handful of games is noise.

Live and backtest are kept apart. The live record starts with the 2026-27 season and counts only predictions published before the event. Backtests replay 2023-24 through 2025-26 and are labeled as such: they show how a model would have done, not calls made at the time.

injuryImpact.title: Injury impact
body: Not a prediction: a count of what injuries have cost each team this season.

A man-game lost is a completed regular-season game in which a player was on his team's injury report that day (ESPN's report, the latest snapshot on or before the game, within a few days) as day-to-day, out or on injured reserve, and didn't dress — checked against the NHL's own shift data. Day-to-day players who played don't count, and suspensions never count.

WAR lost: each missed game is worth the player's wins above replacement per game, from this season and last pooled, once he has at least 20 games. A below-replacement player counts as nothing lost. Goalies count in man-games only. WAR is the app's own calculation from MoneyPuck's player data.
Counting starts with the 2026-27 regular season, because the injury history only begins in September 2026.
limits: Injuries a team never puts on the report can't be seen.
An injured player whose name couldn't be matched to an NHL player only counts when listed out or on injured reserve.

tradeTrees.title: Trade trees
body: Not a prediction: a record of each trade and where every asset went next.

ESPN's transactions feed has no structured trade data — each team posts its side as a sentence. That text is parsed into players, draft picks, rights and future considerations; anything that can't be recognized is shown as written rather than guessed. The two teams' entries are paired when they name each other within two days.

Picks are matched to the NHL's own draft records: the pick whose ownership chain passes directly between the two teams in the stated year and round, or ESPN's own pick number when it's given. Picks that can't be matched are labeled: not drafted yet, not traced (often a conditional pick that was deferred or never conveyed), or can't tell which.

Each asset links to the next trade its new team sent it on in; following those links is what makes the tree. Players are matched to the NHL's player list since 2014-15, so their names open their player card; a name shared by two players is left unmatched.
Covers trades since January 2015, rebuilt every night.
limits: About 3% of assets in older entries are worded in ways that aren't recognized.
A trade ESPN never posted can't appear, and when only one team posted, that team's wording is all there is.

data.title: Data and schedule
body: The pipeline runs every night at 3 AM Eastern. Predictions for today's and tomorrow's games are written in that run, and the playoff odds and injury impact are recomputed then too.
items: NHL API — schedules, results, standings, rosters, box scores and shift charts.
NHL records — every draft pick and who owned it before it was used.
MoneyPuck — player season data used for WAR.

changelog.title: Changelog
body: Dated changes to how the models work, newest first. Each prediction is made by the version in place at the time.

changelogEntries.lineupTest: Tested adjusting game winners for missing players and the starting goalie on past seasons; not adopted (see Game winners).
changelogEntries.tradeTrees: Trade trees added, from ESPN transactions since 2015.
changelogEntries.scorecard: Public scorecard added: game-winner probabilities are logged each morning, and neutral-site games get no home-ice edge.
changelogEntries.startingGoalies: Starting-goalie probabilities added, fit on 2023-24 to 2025-26 starts.
changelogEntries.playoffOdds: Playoff odds added: 10,000 simulated seasons, rating uncertainty tuned on 2023-24 to 2025-26, and a 22.1% overtime rate pooled across those seasons.
changelogEntries.injuryImpact: Injury impact added: man-games and WAR lost per team, counted from the 2026-27 season.
changelogEntries.elo: Game winners switch to Elo (FiveThirtyEight's NHL settings), replacing a hand-weighted formula that backtested worse.

scorecard.title: Prediction scorecard
scorecard.intro: How the app's predictions have actually done, graded against what happened. The live record only counts predictions published before the game; backtests replay past seasons without seeing the results and are labeled as such.
scorecard.howToRead: Picked right: the side given 50% or more is what happened. Brier score measures how close the percentages were: 0 is perfect, 0.25 is what always saying 50% would score. Lower is better.
scorecard.edgeInBrier: Picks the outcome about as often as the baseline; the edge is in how closely the percentages match reality (lower Brier).
scorecard.unavailable: The scorecard isn't available right now.
